description: Plan tasks carry a trust-model change level, and apply refuses to execute auto-fix tasks above the default ceiling (Level 2) unless an explicit, recorded Level 3 override is given, so Level 3 stays advisory-only by default. Handler-reported writes are level-checked after the write (detection, not prevention), and change-scope is bound to the plan being applied.
expectedBehavior: generatePlanContract labels every plan task with changeLevel 1, 2, or 3 derived deterministically from ruleId and the canonical repo-relative file path.

Classification runs on the canonical path: dot segments resolved, backslashes normalized, absolute in-repo paths made repo-relative, trailing dots and spaces stripped per segment, lowercased. Paths that escape the repository are Level 3.
A plan artifact may raise a task's declared changeLevel but can never lower it below the level Playbook classifies from the task itself.
parsePlanArtifact rejects a declared changeLevel that is not 1, 2, or 3.
A rule id outside the reviewed built-in table, and any rule id served by a plugin-registered handler, is never below Level 2.
validateRemediationPlan and FixExecutor.apply reject any auto-fix task above Level 2 before any handler runs.
Non-auto-fix tasks are skipped by apply and are not gated by the ceiling.
After a handler reports applied, each filesChanged path is canonicalized and level-checked; a Level 3 write without the override fails the task and halts the run (remaining tasks are skipped).
The maintenance-plan branch of apply validates its tasks (validateRemediationPlan) before any maintenance command runs.

apply --allow-level 3 --reason "<text>" (both required once each with a value; only 3; reason trimmed, at most 400 chars, a visible non-space character, no control/format/separator characters) raises the ceiling to Level 3 for that run. Library entry points (applyExecutionPlan changeLevelOverride, FixExecutor.apply and validateRemediationPlan maxChangeLevel above 2) require a valid reason and throw without one. The override is rejected with --policy, --policy-check and maintenance-plan execution.

The override is recorded as an apply.change-level-override.v1 memory event written before the executor runs (best-effort, reason secret-redacted) and as changeLevelOverride in the apply result, whose overriddenTaskIds lists every task that passed only because of the override, including tasks caught by the reported-write check.

plan --json stamps its change-scope bundle with source.artifactDigest (sha256 over each task's id, rule, file, action, autoFix, task_kind and hashes of write and preconditions; changeLevel excluded; null and undefined hash alike).

When --from-plan is a plan artifact, apply refuses a change-scope written by another command, without a digest, or with a different digest than the plan being applied. Release, test-fix, docs-consolidation and maintenance plans do not read the change-scope file; without --from-plan the scope limits are enforced with no digest check.
